node.title: Re: You won't believe what this regular expression does!
node.author: haukex
node.doctext: Surprising, yes, but I guess I'd call it a pitfall of both * and a zero-width assertion. s/o*$/O/gm first matches "hello " and the $ assertion is satisfied, and since it's zero-width the matching position is left just before the . Then it matches "hello  " because o* and $ are satisfied, and then the regex engine matches the same thing again but the rules in [doc://perlre#Repeated-Patterns-Matching-a-Zero-length-Substring] kick in, advancing the position past the instead. Update: You can see this in action with: perl -MRegexp::Debugger -e '"hello foo"=~s/o*$/O/gmr' Update 2: Note the same thing happens again with foo - it first replaces oo with O, and then adds the second O because it matched the $ again. You can see this with "o o".
